terms.meaning: An alternate name a company is known by, stored so the company can be matched under each name.
A request that changes data on the server, such as creating or saving.
An automated search for new sources about a company. The code names it, but its details were not reviewed.
A ready-made set of companies that can be imported in one step, judging by the code's names.

sections.name: File setup, SOURCE_TYPES, CompanyTab
sections.title: Imports, source types and tab names
sections.what: Brings in the data calls, layout pieces, icons and the company type list. Also defines the five source kinds and the six tab names.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs these pieces for the lists, forms and source types.
sections.watch_out: The company type list is imported but was not used in the visible part of the file.

sections.name: TAB_CONFIG
sections.title: Which company types go in which tab
sections.what: Maps each tab to the company types it shows. Owners and operators share one tab, and suppliers, regulators, associations, media and others share the last tab.
sections.why: Likely reason: grouping types into tabs makes a long list easier to scan.
sections.watch_out: A company type missing from every tab will not appear anywhere on the page.

sections.name: Companies (part 1)
sections.title: Page state and loading company data
sections.what: Holds the current tab, search text, which company is open, the add-company form, alias and source inputs, discovery status and pack choices. Loads the company list for the industry, the packs when that panel is open, and the full record of the open company.
sections.why: Likely reason: one page holds all the forms and lists together, so the state is kept here.
sections.watch_out: Company data is loaded per industry, so changing the industry must refresh these lists or the old list may stay on screen.

sections.name: Companies: if
sections.title: Filling the profile form and saving edits
sections.what: When a company opens, copies its details into the profile form. Saving trims the values, requires a name, and sends the update. A failed save shows a clear message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form should show the saved values and reject a blank name before any request is sent.
sections.watch_out: The form refills only when the open company's id changes, so a later change to the same company may not reach the form until it is reopened.

sections.name: Companies: if
sections.title: Website check and source and alias actions
sections.what: Checks that a website typed into a company profile is a real web address before the save goes through. It also sets up the actions for adding, switching off, and removing company sources, and for adding and removing aliases (other names a company goes by).
sections.why: Likely reason: the website check stops bad addresses before they reach the server. The action setups sit here so the buttons further down can call them.
sections.watch_out: Changing an alias refreshes only the open company row, so other views may show old data until the page reloads.

sections.name: Companies (part 4)
sections.title: Discovery, pack import and search filtering
sections.what: Starts a discovery run that looks for new companies and sources, either for every company or for one. It then checks the job status every two seconds and refreshes the lists when the job finishes. It also imports a curated company pack and filters the visible companies by the active tab and the search text.
sections.why: Likely reason: discovery runs on the server and can take time, so the page polls the job status instead of waiting for one reply.
sections.watch_out: The polling loop has no time limit, so a job the server never marks as finished keeps the Run Discovery button disabled.

sections.name: Companies (part 5)
sections.title: Tab counts and page header buttons
sections.what: Counts how many companies fall under each tab so every tab can show a number. Draws the page title, the company count, and three buttons: Company Packs, Add Company, and Run Discovery (All), which is disabled while a discovery run is in progress.
sections.why: Likely reason: the counts are stored in a memo so they are recalculated only when the company list changes, not on every screen update.
sections.watch_out: A company type that appears in more than one tab is counted only under the first matching tab.

sections.name: Companies (part 6)
sections.title: Discovery progress banner
sections.what: Shows a coloured banner with the discovery status: a spinner while the job runs, a summary of new, updated, and linked records when it completes, and an error message if it fails. When duplicates were skipped, it lists the reasons in a grid or, for an older response format, as plain text.
sections.why: Likely reason: the summary can arrive in two formats, so the banner checks for both before it shows the skip breakdown.
sections.watch_out: If skip numbers look missing, check which of the two summary formats the server is sending.

sections.name: Companies (part 7)
sections.title: Add company form fields
sections.what: Draws the first part of the Add Company form, with fields for name, type, country, website, headquarters, founded year, and description. The type dropdown lists every company type with underscores replaced by spaces.
sections.why: Likely reason: the form stays hidden until the user clicks Add Company, which keeps the page shorter.
sections.watch_out: The website field is not checked in this section, so any check for new companies depends on code that is not shown here.

sections.name: Companies (part 8)
sections.title: Add button and start of packs panel
sections.what: Finishes the Add Company form with the description box and an Add button that stays disabled until a name is typed or while saving. Then begins the Company Packs panel, which explains that packs are bulk imports that skip duplicates and add new aliases to existing matches.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Add button is greyed out until a name exists, so an empty company is not sent to the server.
sections.watch_out: Packs skip companies that match an existing one by normalized name or domain, so a separate company with a similar name can be skipped.

sections.name: Companies (part 9)
sections.title: Pack cards and industry tabs
sections.what: Shows each pack's count of new and existing companies and its Import button, which reads All Imported when nothing is left to add. Then draws the tab bar, where each tab shows its count. Clicking a tab clears the search box and closes any open company row. The vendors tab is labelled Technology Providers outside the nuclear industry.
sections.why: Likely reason: the nuclear industry keeps the older vendor label, so the new label applies only to other industries.
sections.watch_out: Switching tabs clears the search box, so a user who searched on one tab has to type the search again.

sections.name: Companies (part 10)
sections.title: Search box and company list rows
sections.what: Draws the search box, a loading spinner while data arrives, and one row per company showing its name, country, and website host name. A link on each row opens the company page, and the link address depends on the industry. Clicking the rest of a row opens or closes its details.
sections.why: Likely reason: the link stops the click from also opening the row, so the two actions do not conflict.
sections.watch_out: If a stored website is not a valid address, the row shows the raw text instead of a host name.

sections.name: Companies (part 11)
sections.title: Row badges, discover button and profile fields
sections.what: Shows the source count, project count, and company type on each row, plus a Discover button that runs discovery for only that company. When a row is open, it starts the profile editor with name, type, and country fields and a website field.
sections.why: Likely reason: the Discover button sits on each row so one company can be refreshed without running discovery for all of them.
sections.watch_out: Discover buttons are disabled while any discovery run is in progress, so one long run blocks all of them.

sections.name: Companies (part 12)
sections.title: Rest of profile editor and save
sections.what: Finishes the profile editor with headquarters, founded, and description fields. Shows any profile error in red under the form, and a Save Profile button that is disabled while a save is in progress.
sections.why: Likely reason: errors appear inside the form so the user sees them next to the fields being edited.
sections.watch_out: The website address is checked only when Save is pressed, so a bad address is not flagged while typing.

sections.name: Companies (part 13)
sections.title: Source list and add source inputs
sections.what: Ends the Save Profile button, then draws the list of sources for the company. Each source shows its type, its link, a switch to turn it on or off, a delete button, and the date it was last crawled. Below the list are a type dropdown and a URL box for adding a new source.
sections.why: Likely reason: each source has its own on and off switch, so a source can be paused without being deleted.
sections.watch_out: The on and off switch and the delete button act right away, with no confirmation step.

sections.name: Companies (part 14)
sections.title: Add source button and alias list
sections.what: Draws the Add button for sources, which stays disabled until a URL is typed. Then shows the company's aliases as small tags, each with an X to remove it, followed by a text box where a new alias is added by pressing Enter or the Add button.
sections.why: Likely reason: aliases are short, so they are shown as small removable tags rather than in a table.
sections.watch_out: The alias text box is shared by all company rows, so a half-typed alias can carry over to a different row.

sections.name: Companies (part 15)
sections.title: Linked projects and empty-list messages
sections.what: Shows a grid of the projects linked to the company, with each project's name and the company's role in it, but only when links exist. Also shows a message when no companies match the current tab or search text, and the wording changes depending on whether a search is active.
sections.why: Likely reason: the different wording tells the user whether to clear the search or change the tab.

summary: The Companies admin page: lists companies for the current industry in tabs by type, and lets users add companies, edit profiles, and manage aliases, sources, discovery and company packs.
purpose: Lets staff keep the company list accurate for owners, builders, vendors and others.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the overall layout. The visible parts show one tab per company type.
how: 1. Loads the companies for the current industry. 2. Sorts them into tabs by type. 3. Loads a company's full record when it is opened. 4. Saves profile edits through the server. 5. Other features, such as aliases, sources, discovery and packs, are in sections that were not reviewed.
inputs: The current industry, the company list and details from the server, and what the user types into forms.
outputs: Tabs of companies, a profile form, error messages when a save fails, and new companies when created.
risks: Saves go to the server straight away. A company type missing from the tab list will not appear under any tab. Only 4 of 17 sections were available to review.
debug: If a company is missing from every tab, compare its type with the tab list. If a save fails, read the message under the profile form and check the browser's network log. If the form shows old data, check the id of the company that is open.
